Islands, biomes and world generations

This page explains the shape of a world: the sea and its islands, the starting island, the biomes you can find, and why a saved world keeps its own terrain.

Updated 8 November 2026 · 3 min read · Everyone · feature ledger · all guides
Contents
  1. The endless sea and its islands
  2. 92 biomes
  3. World generations
  4. How this was checked

The endless sea and its islands

A world is an endless sea. Island groups sit in it, and open ocean separates one group from the next. Endless archipelago and the starting island

  • Small islands and palm-ringed coral atolls.
  • Regional and great islands.
  • Continental landmasses, the largest of all.

Many islands have up to eight small satellite islets offshore, across a strait of roughly 240 m or more. Atolls have none.

Your world begins on the starting island, at X 0, Z 0. You start in a meadow clearing that blends into the island's own biomes a few hundred metres out. The starting island's terrain is gentler than other islands, and it very rarely has a volcano.

92 biomes

A world has 92 named biomes. They range from meadows, orchards and bamboo thickets to salt flats, kelp forests, meteor fields and surface lava tubes. Every one of them can appear in a new world. 92 biomes

Each biome has its own ground, plants and trees. Forests mix a leading tree with a few others: oak in Dense forest, redwoods in Coastal redwood forest and cypress in Blackwater bayou, for example. Coral atolls grow palms. The animals you meet also depend on the biome. Where and how many animals appear

The FPS and coordinates readout shows the biome you are in, after BIOME. The map locator can find any of the 92 biomes, so you can travel to one you have not seen yet. See the maps guide for how to set a destination.

World generations

Each world keeps the terrain rules it was made with, called its generation. In Create world, the Terrain generation field starts at 12, the current rules. Click it or press Left or Right to pick an earlier generation, back to 1 (Legacy). World generations (terrain rule versions)

A saved world keeps its generation when it loads, so an update does not reshape land you have already built on. The Worlds list shows each save's generation after its mode, for example 'Creative / Gen 12'.

Good to know. Expedition sites need generation 10 or later. In an older world, the Journal says "Landmarks appear in new generation-10 worlds" instead of listing sites. Expedition sites and one-time supply finds

A generation 1 world cannot contain meteor fields, surface lava tubes or amethyst gorges. Its map locator marks them with * and UNAVAILABLE IN THIS WORLD. To see them, create a new world.

How this guide was checked

Re-checked against the Voxelgame 251b9e46 source on 8 November 2026. Island tiers, atolls, continental pairs and satellite islets: crates/voxelgame-core/src/world/generator/archipelago.rs and the spacing constants in world/generator.rs. Spawn at X 0, Z 0: game.rs. The starting meadow and gentler starting island: generator/biomes.rs and generator/terrain_profile.rs. Biome::ALL (92 entries), generated_naturally() and the names: world/generator.rs; tree mixes: generator/trees.rs. Map locator catalogue and generation-1 limits: map_locator.rs and crates/voxelgame-render/src/map_locator_ui.rs. Generations: GeneratorVersion (Current = 12) in world/generator.rs, game/startup_create.rs, src/local_startup.rs, save/load.rs and the Create world and Worlds screens in crates/voxelgame-render/src/startup_ui.rs and startup_ui/worlds.rs.

Initial ledger audit: Voxelgame main dd29d91, committed 10 October 2026; article updated 8 November 2026. Source-checked at Voxelgame 251b9e46 on 8 November 2026; not play-tested. Island sizes are internal envelope values, so the tiers are described, not measured. Biome locations depend on the seed, so this page gives no map positions. The island atlas and survey pages show older generations and builds.
